overview: Published in 1594 as a graver companion to Venus and Adonis (again dedicated to Southampton), this 1855-line poem retells a foundational Roman story from Livy and Ovid. Sextus Tarquinius, son of the tyrant king, is inflamed by the chastity of Lucrece, wife of his comrade Collatine. He rides to her house, is received as a guest, and rapes her at knife-point that night. Overwhelmed with shame, Lucrece summons her husband and father, reveals the crime, exacts their oath of revenge, and stabs herself. Her kinsman Brutus turns the outrage into revolution: the Tarquins are expelled and Rome becomes a republic. In grave rhyme-royal stanzas the poem dwells on the psychology of lust and guilt and on Lucrece's long laments. (The poem depicts sexual assault and suicide.)

acts.summary: Tarquin's lust, the rape of Lucrece, her laments and suicide, and Brutus's revolt that expels the kings and founds the Republic.
